texts: In a young man with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who needs a septal myectomy, sudden death in his father and a cousin at a young age is an indication for an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator as well.
Sudden death in a close relative is a major risk factor in HCM, along with unexplained syncope, massive wall thickness of 30 mm or more, non-sustained VT and an apical aneurysm.
Myectomy relieves the obstruction and usually abolishes the systolic anterior motion and the mitral regurgitation it causes, so the mitral valve needs no replacement or ring.
Relieving the obstruction does not remove the risk of arrhythmia.
In the picture, Usopp chisels the thick wall while the bodyguard steps in, and the two coffins stand behind.
Memory hook: two coffins in the family photo: chisel the wall and hire the bodyguard.
